name: separated_toffoli_pair_temporary_and_sharing
precondition: dv_recon / Toffoli-level IRCircuit: needs toffoli (ccz or ccx present), needs ancilla_room, measurement allowed; qubits <= 24. Requires at least two ccz/ccx gates that share a control pair (shared_control_pairs > 0). No rotations required.
identity: Let g_i = CCZ(x,y,z) at position i and g_j = CCZ(x,y,z') at a LATER position j (for ccx, z/z' is the target; for ccz pick any wire as the 'target' and the other two as the AND pair), with the SAME unordered pair {x,y} as AND pair. Suppose no gate strictly between i and j writes x or y (x,y may be read as controls, i.e. appear as a control of cx/cz/ccz, but never as a cx/ccx target, x, h, or measurement target). Then the value a = x AND y is constant over the whole span [i, j]. Rewrite: insert and_compute(x, y -> a) on a fresh clean ancilla a immediately before position i (4 T), replace g_i by cz(a, z) (or cx(a, z) for ccx), leave every op in between untouched, replace g_j by cz(a, z') (resp. cx(a, z')), and insert and_uncompute(a) immediately after position j (0 T: measure a in the X basis, classically controlled cz(x,y) fix-up). Cost: 4 T for the pair instead of 7 + 7 = 14 T. The construction generalises to a chain of k same-AND-pair gates in the span, giving 4 T for all k instead of 7k. Spans are processed greedily longest-first; overlapping spans with different AND pairs each get their own ancilla (ancillas are reused once their span closes), nested spans are allowed.
correctness: CCZ(x,y,z) = CZ(a,z) and CCX(x,y;z) = CX(a;z) whenever the ancilla a holds the Boolean x AND y, on every computational basis state, with no phase: both are diagonal/permutation operators whose action depends only on the product x*y. Gidney's temporary-AND gadget (arXiv:1709.06648) computes a = x AND y on a clean |0> ancilla with 4 T and T-depth 1, and uncomputes it with zero T by measuring the ancilla in the X basis and applying a classically controlled CZ(x,y) to clear the measurement-induced phase kickback; the uncompute is exact, restores a to |0>, and is correct for ARBITRARY superpositions of x,y because the correction is itself controlled on x,y. The only hypothesis needed is that x and y are unwritten on the span, which makes a = x AND y an invariant there; the intervening ops may freely read x, y, and read or write z, because each original gate is replaced in place by an equivalent two-qubit gate at exactly its own position, so the operator ordering of the whole circuit is unchanged. The accepted rule and_ancilla_ccz_lowering_with_measured_uncompute is the special case where the gates are ADJACENT (a run); this is why it leaves adder_6 at 11 x 7 = 77 T. The relaxation 'controls unwritten' rather than 'nothing in between' is the whole content of the idea, and it is exactly the compute/uncompute structure of a ripple-carry adder: the carry Toffoli and its mirror image share the same control pair, and only the carry wire is touched in between.
trigger: Scan the op list for ccz/ccx gates. Group them by unordered AND-pair candidate: for ccx take {controls}; for ccz take all three 2-subsets of its wires. For each candidate pair {x,y} and each pair of occurrences i < j in its occurrence list, accept the span if (a) no op in (i, j) has x or y as a WRITTEN qubit - written = cx/ccx target, x, h, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz, measure, or either wire of a non-diagonal gate - and (b) a clean ancilla is available (append_ancillas). Emit one match per maximal such span, with the list of member gate positions, preferring the span covering the most ccz/ccx gates; matches are emitted in order of decreasing member count and the runner applies them one at a time, re-triggering after each.
expected_effect: adder_6 has 11 ccz and fingerprint reports 5 shared_control_pairs, i.e. 5 compute/uncompute carry pairs plus one unpaired ccz. Each qualifying pair falls from 14 T to 4 T. If all 5 pairs qualify: 5*4 + 7 = 27 T (saving 50). Conservatively assuming 4 of the 5 spans survive the 'controls unwritten' test and the remaining 3 ccz stay at 7 T: 4*4 + 21 = 37 T (saving 40). Qubits rise by the number of simultaneously open spans (at most 5, so 14 -> at most 19) and CNOT count rises slightly, but cost order is lexicographic in (T, qubits, CNOT), so the T drop decides. This also crosses the best baseline, pyzx at 47, which is unitary-only and cannot use measurement.
source: Craig Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (temporary-AND / measurement-based uncompute); Cuccaro, Draper, Kutin, Moulton, quant-ph/0410184 (ripple-carry MAJ/UMA compute-uncompute pairing)
